The starter is ready when it is bubbly, active, and has a pleasant sour smell.

text: The Black Forest is a wooded mountain range in the state of Baden-Württemberg in southwestern Germany. It covers an area of approximately 6,000 square kilometres and has a highest point of 1,493 metres at the Feldberg. The region is known for its dark, dense fir and spruce forests, traditional farmhouses, cuckoo clocks, Black Forest gateau, and the source of the Danube and Neckar rivers.

text: Pancake Day, or Shrove Tuesday, falls 47 days before Easter Sunday and marks the last day before the Christian fasting season of Lent begins. In the United Kingdom, it is a tradition to make and eat pancakes on this day. The name 'Shrove' comes from the practice of confessing sins, or being 'shriven', before Lent. Pancake races, in which participants run while tossing pancakes in a frying pan, are a common community event.

text: The mute swan is the largest native bird in the United Kingdom and one of the heaviest flying birds in the world. Adult birds have an entirely white plumage and an orange bill with a distinctive black knob at the base. Mute swans mate for life and typically live for 10 to 15 years. They are found on rivers, lakes, and estuaries and feed mainly on aquatic vegetation.

text: The Sahel is a semi-arid transitional zone in Africa stretching approximately 5,400 kilometres from the Atlantic coast of Senegal in the west to Eritrea in the east. It lies between the Sahara Desert to the north and the more fertile savannas and forests to the south. The region experiences variable rainfall and is subject to periodic drought. It covers parts of Senegal, Mauritania, Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, Nigeria, Chad, Sudan, and Eritrea.

text: The domestic dog is a domesticated descendant of the grey wolf and one of the most widely kept companion animals in the world. Dogs were the first species to be domesticated by humans, with the process beginning between 15,000 and 40,000 years ago. There are estimated to be over 340 officially recognised breeds, varying greatly in size, coat type, and temperament. Dogs are used for a wide range of working roles in addition to being kept as pets.

text: The Henley Royal Regatta is an annual rowing event held on the River Thames at Henley-on-Thames in Oxfordshire, typically taking place over five days in late June or early July. It was first held in 1839 and is one of the most prestigious rowing events in the world. Competitors race in a straight one-mile and 550-yard course. The event is as well known for its social atmosphere and dress code as for the rowing itself.

The Highlands are known for their dramatic scenery, traditional culture, and Gaelic heritage, as well as activities including walking, climbing, fishing, and whisky distilling.

text: The Mariana Trench is the deepest oceanic trench on Earth, located in the western Pacific Ocean to the east of the Mariana Islands. Its deepest point, known as the Challenger Deep, is approximately 11,000 metres below sea level. The trench was formed by the subduction of the Pacific Plate beneath the Mariana Plate. Despite its extreme depth, pressure, and darkness, the trench harbours specialised microbial and invertebrate life.

The course runs 42.195 kilometres from Hopkinton to Copley Square in downtown Boston.

The valley is home to numerous Renaissance châteaux and was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.

text: The Dolomites are a mountain range in northeastern Italy forming part of the Southern Limestone Alps. It is also home to large populations of bison, wolves, grizzly bears, and elk.

Male platypuses have a venomous spur on their hind legs. It is one of the few mammals capable of detecting electrical fields using its bill.

It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most visited archaeological sites in the world.
